The Pursuit of AGI Resolves the Three-Body Problem in Computing

Big software disasters hide in unwritten guesses between theorists, builders, and users—machine-checked handoffs lock the stack.

[Checked Handoffs Stop Bug Cascades Cold]

1/3 Most major computer failures start at the handoffs between teams or system layers, not inside individual parts.

2/3 The culprit is usually an unwritten guess crossing a boundary, such as which physical units a number uses.

3/3 When every boundary guess is written down and machine-checked, fixing one problem stays fixed without breaking upper layers.
